title: Switching _run_turn from query() to ClaudeSDKClient hung indefinitely in prod
description:
Attempted fix for the MCP-server-startup race (calendar tools not indexed
yet when the model's first turn started - see the commit this reverts,
d1744b6, "wait for MCP servers to leave pending before sending the
turn's prompt"). The approach: replace the one-shot query() call in
_run_turn with an explicit ClaudeSDKClient - connect(), poll
get_mcp_status() until every catalog server left "pending" (wrapped in
asyncio.timeout(45.0) as a backstop), then client.query(prompt) and
client.receive_response().

Passed ruff/ty/fast pytest/--container. Deployed to prod. The very next
real turn hung for 16+ minutes with no response and no error - it never
reached a terminal state, which (per Registry.begin) would have wedged
every subsequent turn on the instance indefinitely once discovered.
Reverted immediately (e44812b) and redeployed; healthz confirmed
busy=false afterward.

The 45s asyncio.timeout on the polling loop should have fired long
before 16 minutes, which means the hang was NOT in _wait_for_mcp_ready's
poll loop - the more likely suspect is client.connect() or
client.query()/receive_response() itself never returning. One candidate:
ClaudeSDKClient's own docstring warning - "you cannot use a
ClaudeSDKClient instance across different async runtime contexts (e.g.,
different trio nurseries or asyncio task groups) ... internally
maintains a persistent anyio task group ... must complete all operations
within the same async context where it was connected." Worth checking
whether _run_turn's caller (turns.py/main.py's turn dispatch) runs each
turn in a context that could violate that constraint - a bare query()
call apparently tolerates something ClaudeSDKClient does not.

Before retrying this approach: reproduce locally first under --container
or --live with a deliberately slow/misbehaving MCP server, with a
task-level timeout wrapping the whole turn (not just the wait helper) so
a repeat of this failure mode degrades to an error turn instead of an
indefinite hang. The underlying race (img mentioned in commit cb20583's
prompt-text mitigation, which is still in place and NOT reverted) may be
enough on its own without touching the query()/ClaudeSDKClient boundary.

title: PostgresSessionStore never persists: agent_sessions has 0 rows on prod despite healthz=ready
description:
/healthz reports transcripts=ready, meaning PostgresSessionStore.start()
connected successfully - but querying agent_sessions on prod's own
SESSION_DATABASE_URL directly (via flyctl ssh) returns 0 rows, despite
multiple real turns having run (POST /api/turns 202, ListToolsRequest,
loaded workspace guide, etc. all logged).

"ready" in /healthz only proves the pool connected at startup
(app/main.py _start_session_store). It says nothing about whether the SDK
is actually calling register()/append() on the store during a turn.
session_store.py's own docstring flags this as a real risk: "the SDK's
SessionStore protocol is small but versioned; if your SDK release expects
different method names, adapt here." claude-agent-sdk is pinned
>=0.2.0,<0.3.0 in requirements.txt; worth checking whether the installed
version's SessionStore protocol still matches the method names
PostgresSessionStore implements (register/append), on both the local dev
venv (found 0.1.68 installed, NOT satisfying the pin) and whatever
requirements.txt actually resolves to on prod's built image.

Found while investigating why the calendar MCP tools appeared unavailable
to the agent (a separate issue) - wanted the real transcript for that turn
and discovered there's no transcript data to read at all.

title: [bug] We pin bd 1.2.1, which upstream retracted as an accidental untested release
description:
Found while diagnosing img-523. Separate defect, larger blast radius.

WHAT UPSTREAM SAYS

The Dockerfile pins BEADS_VERSION=1.2.1. That release is now marked prerelease
with: 'This release was published by accident and is untested. Do not use it.'
v1.2.2 supersedes it by re-releasing the tested v1.1.2 code under a higher
number, and go.mod retracts 1.2.1/1.2.0/1.1.1. So every ledger in this system --
this repo's, and every per-user graph on the volume -- is held by a binary its
author withdrew.

THE SCHEMA TRAP, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED

Running 1.2.1 even once migrates the database v53 -> v65. Against a COPY of this
repo's .beads:
  - pinned 1.2.1: reads fine
  - v1.2.2 darwin_arm64: refuses, 'database is at v65, binary knows up to v53
    (12 migrations ahead)'
  - v1.2.2 --ignore-schema-skew: reads all 21 issues fine

So bumping BEADS_VERSION to 1.2.2 ships a binary that REFUSES every existing
prod ledger. Downgrading is not a version bump; it needs a per-database Dolt
cursor rollback (docs/RECOVERY-1.2.1.md): dolt sql -q 'DELETE FROM
schema_migrations WHERE version > 53' plus a DOLT_COMMIT, in
.beads/embeddeddolt/<db>, for this repo AND each user dir on the volume, reached
through scripts/fly.sh --write. Needs the dolt CLI, which the image does not have.

WHY CI WOULD NOT CATCH IT -- the part that makes this P1

Two mechanisms hide it:
  1. The container tier builds FRESH ledgers. 1.2.2 creates those at v53 and
     opens them happily, so the tier goes green.
  2. kb.py deliberately logs-and-continues when beads is unreachable, because a
     turn that cannot reach its ledger should still answer the user.
Together: a green suite, a deploy that looks healthy, turns that keep answering,
and a ledger silently recording nothing. That is precisely the silence the
container tier was built to break, arriving underneath it.

OPTIONS

  a) Stay on 1.2.1 deliberately, and say in the Dockerfile that the pin is now
     load-bearing for a second reason (the v65 schema) and not just the first.
     Cost: all task state on code upstream calls untested.
  b) Coordinated downgrade to 1.2.2: recover every database, then bump. Note
     1.2.2 drops the 1.2.x-only features (work leases, events journal, sync
     federation, HTTP API, provenance events) -- confirm we use none before
     committing to this.
  c) Wait for a properly tested 1.2.x and do it once.

Whichever way, do NOT bump the pin as a routine dependency update. A test that
opens a v65 database with the pinned binary would turn this from a landmine into
a failure, and is probably worth having either way.
notes:
Repo half done (see Dockerfile, fly.toml, CLAUDE.md). Pin moved 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2 with BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1 in fly.toml as the bridge; local bd upgraded.

MEASURED, on a copy of this repo's ledger:
- 1.2.2 refuses the v65 db exactly as reported.
- Cursor rollback (upstream docs/RECOVERY-1.2.1.md, which is UPSTREAM's file, not ours - this bead cited it as if we had it) is lossless: full --json dump of all 22 issues byte-identical to 1.2.1's, dep edges intact, bd ready identical at 10. Writes work after.
- The stopgap is the env var BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1, NOT a --ignore-schema-skew flag as this bead said. It is also not read-only: under it 1.2.2 creates, notes, closes, exports and computes ready against v65, cursor unchanged.

ORDERING HAZARD, and it is asymmetric:
This repo sets sync.remote in .beads/config.yaml, so a leftover 1.2.1 hits the remote-migrate gate and refuses to write - loud. Prod's per-user ledgers have NO remote, so there 1.2.1 would silently re-migrate a rolled-back db. So the image must ship 1.2.2 BEFORE any volume ledger is rolled back.

REMAINING:
1. Roll back this repo's own .beads cursor (blocked in-session by a tool classifier on the DELETE; command handed to the user).
2. Deploy, then roll back each volume ledger via scripts/fly.sh --write. Image has no dolt binary - unresolved how to get one there for a one-time recovery.
3. Drop BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW from fly.toml once every ledger is v53.
DONE. Both ledgers are bd 1.2.2 at Dolt schema v53; BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW is out of fly.toml and prod confirms it unset with no skew warning.

Order used (the hazard is asymmetric, so this order is load-bearing): deploy 1.2.2 first, because prod's ledger has no sync.remote and a leftover 1.2.1 would have silently re-migrated a recovered database. Then back up, then roll the cursor back.

Verified lossless twice, by full export compared record-for-record: 22/22 on this repo's ledger, 16/16 on prod, ids and every field identical, dep edges and bd ready unchanged.

Mechanism: bd sql CANNOT do this - 'not yet supported in embedded mode', and embedded is what runs here. Used dolt 2.3.1 in the container's /tmp, sha256 matched against the same tarball fetched locally, discarded by the next redeploy. dolt was deliberately NOT added to the image.

Also applied upstream's optional follow-up to re-track the audit events table, on both ledgers.

Backups retained on the volume at /work (outside the agent's scratch so it does not trip on them): beads-backup-pre-recovery-dev_localhost, pre-recovery-dev_localhost.jsonl, post-recovery.jsonl. Delete when you are satisfied.

Not done, and separate: img-hiq (port app/mcp_server.py to mcp 2.x; the pin is capped at <2.0.0 for now).
close_reason: recovery complete: both ledgers at v53 on 1.2.2, bridge removed (538af3f)

title: Google tokens expire weekly on a consumer account, and /healthz cannot see it
description:
--- Verification was priced and rejected (2026-08-17) ---

For RESTRICTED scopes it needs: a public homepage on a domain you own verified
via Search Console, a privacy policy on that domain, an unlisted YouTube video
demonstrating each scope, and an ANNUAL CASA Tier 2 assessment - a third-party
DAST scan of the PRODUCTION app, ~$800-6000/yr, several weeks each round.

Google does exempt this shape of app: 'if you are the only user of your app or
if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to
you'. But that exempts VERIFICATION, not the timer - it permits staying in
Testing and clicking through the warning, and Testing is what expires refresh
tokens after 7 days.

So the fork is unchanged and Workspace Internal is the answer: no verification,
no warning screen, no timer, one seat on a household-owned domain. Still no code
changes either way.

--- Verification was priced and rejected (2026-08-17) ---

For RESTRICTED scopes it needs: a public homepage on a domain you own verified
via Search Console, a privacy policy on that domain, an unlisted YouTube video
demonstrating each scope, and an ANNUAL CASA Tier 2 assessment - a third-party
DAST scan of the PRODUCTION app, roughly 800-6000 USD/yr, several weeks each
round.

Google does exempt this shape of app: "if you are the only user of your app or
if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to
you". But that exempts VERIFICATION, not the timer - it permits staying in
Testing and clicking through the warning, and Testing is what expires refresh
tokens after 7 days.

So the fork is unchanged and Workspace Internal is the answer: no verification,
no warning screen, no timer, one seat on a household-owned domain. Still no code
changes either way - only which account consents.
--- Priced (2026-08-17) ---

Workspace Business Starter: $7/user/month annual, $8.40 monthly. ONE seat, so
~$84/yr. That is the floor and it is a real floor: Internal user type needs the
Cloud project attached to a Workspace OR Cloud Identity organisation, and Cloud
Identity Free ($0, 50 users) would supply the org but its accounts are
identity-only - no Gmail, no Calendar, so nothing for the servers to read.

The cost that is not money: Internal means only org members may consent, so the
household identity moves from vogleragent@gmail.com to one on the owned domain.
Everyone re-shares calendars, forwarding filters re-point, re-run
scripts/google-auth.sh, re-set the secrets. No code changes.

Two things that make the seat worth more than it looks. Internal apps do not
list scopes on the consent screen at all and restricted scopes need no review,
so the gmail.compose problem stops existing. And Workspace is the tier where
domain-wide delegation exists - the mechanism consumer Gmail refused - which is
the route to PER-PERSON mailboxes (img-n7g) rather than one shared inbox, at a
seat per person.

Status: both auth flows succeeded 2026-08-17 on the consumer account, so the
current tokens expire around 2026-08-24. Running on that deliberately, to find
out whether the integration earns the seat before buying one.
close_reason:
The code half is shipped: /healthz reports state (missing/ready/expiring/expired) plus a separate refresh verdict, from two signals - a countdown off the stored expiry_date and a real refresh_token POST to Google. The chat page warns on load. Read from the environment variable rather than the materialised file, because the servers write refreshed tokens back to those files and a countdown derived from one never counts down.

Deliberately NOT closed by this: the account decision. User chose to stay on Testing and re-auth weekly rather than buy a Workspace seat, so the seven-day clock stands and img-udo covers the fact that nothing reminds anyone. A dead credential also still does not drop the server, on purpose - see the ADR 0015 amendment.

title: Concurrent turns share one savepoint over one workspace
description:
ADR 0009 says this "is filed rather than fixed here". It was filed nowhere -
the ledger holding it was destroyed - so this is the bead the ADR promised.

`create_savepoint` is `git add -A` and a commit over the single shared
workspace at `$KB_MOUNT/memory`. The savepoint *name* is per turn; the content
is global. `POST /api/turns` has no concurrency guard - reflection has one,
ordinary turns do not.

So two turns in flight at once, from two browser tabs on one machine, already
interleave: one turn's half-written files are swept into the other's savepoint,
and reverting either rolls back both. This is a correctness bug today, at one
machine.

It is also the ceiling ADR 0009 identifies: throughput cannot drive a second
machine, because this is hit first and a second machine makes it worse. Fix it
before anything in 0009's "if the constraint has to go" ordering - scope
savepoints per user, or serialize turns per workspace.

Revert is what makes writing to the wiki reviewable (ADR 0003) and bounded
self-modification defensible at all (ADR 0008, "one click from gone"). This bug
weakens that guarantee while leaving the button in place.
close_reason: one turn at a time via Registry.begin; per-user savepoint scoping filed as follow-up

title: TigerFS has no read-modify-write: a shell append destroys the file
description:
Cited in app/guards.py. Opening a file on the KB mount yields a zero-filled
buffer, and on close that buffer becomes the whole file - so anything not
written in that session is zeroed before the write and truncated after it.

This destroyed a user's memory/CLAUDE.md: an agent hit a file-tool error,
misdiagnosed it, fell back to a shell append, and turned 233 bytes of personal
notes into 233 zeroes while the write reported success.

Shipped: the PreToolUse guard in app/guards.py refuses shell writes into the KB
and names the safe alternative, because a bare denial is what drove the agent
into inventing the workaround in the first place. See ADR 0007 and
skills/kb-curator/references/tigerfs.md.

Reconstructed from the code comment and closed as already delivered.

title: Decide whether signal data justifies Stage 3
description:
Cited in CLAUDE.md as the bead that gates Stage 3 (bounded self-evolution) on
looking at real signal data first, rather than on the design being appealing.

Reconstructed from documentation. The original lived in a local Docker volume
and was destroyed by a `docker compose down -v`; the beads it blocked are gone
with it, so any blocking edge here is rebuilt from what the docs record, not
recovered.

The gate was overridden once already, honestly and on purpose: ADR 0008 records
that the ledger held 6 turns and 0 reverts, and the user chose to ship Stage 3
anyway with a manual `POST /api/reflect` trigger, so that a signal-only path
would not ship unexercised self-modification.

It stays open because the question it asks is still unanswered: `GET
/api/signals` now reports per-skill outcome rates, and nobody has read them in
bulk. Prod currently holds exactly one signal bead (kb-fme, a Bash permission
denial). That is not yet evidence.

title: @agent addressing so two household members can talk without spending a turn
description: In the new household-shared conversation model (docs/decisions/0017), every message that reaches POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages starts or injects into an agent turn - there is no way for two people to talk to each other in the same conversation without every message being sent to the model. Only messages addressed to the agent (or sent while it is already mid-turn) should start/continue a turn; the rest should be persisted and broadcast to the conversation like any other event, and folded into context for the next real turn. This is Phase 5 of the design behind 0017 and was explicitly scoped out as a backlog item, not a commitment.

title: Auto-title conversations after the first exchange
description: docs/decisions/0017 shipped household-shared, durable conversations but no auto-titling: the conversation picker shows 'Untitled — <timestamp>' until PATCH /api/conversations/{id} is called by hand. One cheap model call after the first turn completes should set a title. PATCH /api/conversations/{id} already accepts {title}. Filed as follow-up from kb-nb4, which asked for this but was closed on the core persistence/resumability delivery alone.

title: [bug] mcp is capped below 2.0; port app/mcp_server.py to the 2.x surface
description:
requirements.txt now says mcp>=1.9.0,<2.0.0. Found because the image stopped booting: mcp 2.0.0 deletes mcp.server.fastmcp, which app/mcp_server.py imports, so uvicorn died on ModuleNotFoundError before loading the app and /healthz never opened a port to say so. Every container test errored at setup; fly deploy would have failed the same way.

The cap restores the tested state and is not a fix. 2.x replaces FastMCP with mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer (mcp.server.transport_security, also imported, still exists). Porting needs a read of the new API plus a check that the /mcp streamable-HTTP mount and the hand-rolled auth still behave, since a mounted ASGI app does not run FastAPI dependencies (ADR 0014).

Worth pairing with a wider look at requirements.txt: every dependency there is >= with no upper bound, so this can happen again with fastapi, uvicorn or the agent SDK. The Dockerfile pins bd and Node exactly and explains why; Python deps get none of that.

title: core.hooksPath points at .beads/hooks, so .git/hooks never fires
description:
git config core.hooksPath = <repo>/.beads/hooks

core.hooksPath REPLACES .git/hooks rather than adding to it. beads set it when it
installed its own pre-commit/pre-push/post-merge/post-checkout hooks, and the side
effect is that anything in .git/hooks is dead.

CLAUDE.md tells the reader to run `pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install`.

CORRECTION to this bead as originally filed: it claimed pre-commit writes a hook
that then never executes, silently. It does not. pre-commit checks for
core.hooksPath and refuses:

  [ERROR] Cowardly refusing to install hooks with `core.hooksPath` set.
  hint: `git config --unset-all core.hooksPath`

So nothing was ever silently skipped; the documented step simply could not
succeed, and this repo's .git/hooks held only samples. Milder than filed, and
still a real defect: CLAUDE.md documented a local static gate that no clone could
install, leaving CI as the only check.

Ruled out: pre-commit has no flag to write elsewhere (no --hooks-path, no
--git-dir), and unsetting core.hooksPath would disable beads' hooks to enable
ours.
close_reason: scripts/install-hooks.sh installs the gate into whatever core.hooksPath names, sharing the file with beads' own marked block; scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh is the versioned gate. .pre-commit-config.yaml deleted - the framework refuses under core.hooksPath and was a third pin site. Bead description amended first: pre-commit refuses loudly, it does not silently skip.

title: Review the two Google MCP packages on every version bump
description:
app/mcp_catalog.py pins @cocal/google-calendar-mcp and @klodr/gmail-mcp in the
Dockerfile, and CATALOG classifies every tool they register into auto_approve /
falls-through / deny.

A version bump can add TOOLS. A new one lands in none of those tuples and so
falls through to can_use_tool, which is the safe landing spot - but it means a
tool nobody reviewed is being offered to a person as an Allow/Deny, and a new
SENDING tool would not be in deny.

tests/test_mcp_catalog.py has INVENTORY, measured by booting each server inside
the real image against fake credentials and calling tools/list.
test_every_tool_is_deliberately_placed fails if the tuples and INVENTORY drift,
so a bump breaks the build rather than passing quietly - but only if INVENTORY
is re-measured. That is this bead.

On a bump: re-measure INVENTORY the same way, classify anything new, and check
whether the scope set still matches (@klodr registers tools by granted scope, so
a bump could expose tools the existing token already permits).

Reading the source is NOT enough - it missed manage-accounts and
respond-to-event on the calendar server the first time.

Also worth a look: @klodr/gmail-mcp is ~230 downloads/week and holds a live
mailbox token in a subprocess no PreToolUse hook covers (docs/decisions/0015).

title: README sent operators into a tunnel that cannot work here, and a pre-June Cloudflare UI
description:
Found while setting up Access on the live deployment, 2026-08-15. Two defects in the deploy instructions, both of which cost real time:

1. Step 4 told the operator to create a Cloudflare Tunnel and set TUNNEL_TOKEN, with Access enforced at the tunnel ingress. entrypoint.sh does start cloudflared when that token is present, but the tunnel runs inside the machine while fly.toml sets auto_stop_machines=suspend and min_machines_running=0. Suspended, the tunnel is down, and the only thing that wakes the machine is the Fly proxy receiving a request on the route the tunnel was meant to replace. It cannot recover on its own. The README also gave the ingress config as YAML (access: {required: true, ...}), which a --token tunnel cannot use at all since it is remotely managed.

2. Step 3 pointed at the pre-June-2026 dashboard. Identity providers moved to Zero Trust > Integrations > Identity providers, and as of 2026-06-18 new accounts get the Cloudflare identity provider by default with One-time PIN no longer added automatically. That matters beyond navigation: the Cloudflare provider only admits members of your Cloudflare account, so a household member on an outside address cannot log in until OTP or a social IdP is added.

Fixed in this commit: README steps 3 and 4 rewritten to cover DNS/cert ordering (grey cloud, fly certs add, then orange cloud + Full strict), the current IdP path, the two-policy split (Allow for people, Service Auth for /mcp), and an explicit section on why there is no tunnel. app/auth.py's module docstring no longer promises a tunnel-ingress second layer it does not have.

Still open, and the reason this is filed rather than just committed: the tunnel code path in entrypoint.sh is now documented as unusable under the default fly.toml. Decide whether to delete it, or keep it and have the entrypoint refuse to start cloudflared when min_machines_running is 0 rather than silently starting a tunnel that dies at the first idle timeout.
close_reason: cloudflared removed from image and entrypoint; a leftover TUNNEL_TOKEN now warns

title: bd ready silently ignores cross-prefix blocking edges
description:
This ledger holds two prefixes by design: kb- beads pulled from the volume (ids preserved as the join key) and img- beads created here. A blocking edge BETWEEN the two prefixes is accepted, stored, and displayed — bd show, bd dep tree and bd ready --explain all render it — but bd ready does not honour it. The blocked issue is reported ready, with --explain claiming 'N blocker(s) resolved' and naming an open blocker as resolved.

Reproduced repeatedly on 2026-08-14:
- kb-b82 depending on an img- bead: reported ready, blocker listed as resolved. Survived removing and re-adding the edge canonically with bd dep add, and survived bd export.
- img-n7g depending on kb-b82 (open, itself blocked): same.
- Controls all behave correctly: a same-prefix pair blocks, and a clean same-prefix three-link chain blocks at both levels.

Why it matters: CLAUDE.md names bd ready the source of truth for what is open, and the failure is silent in the direction that loses work — an edge that looks wired lets blocked work surface as claimable. Live instance: img-n7g is blocked by kb-b82 in intent and in its description, but shows up in bd ready.

Next step is to find whether this is a bd version issue (check the pin in the Dockerfile against upstream) or something about how beads-pull.sh imports foreign-prefix ids. Until then, treat a cross-prefix edge as documentation only and state the ordering in the description, as img-n7g does.
close_reason:
Diagnosed. Not ours to fix, and not a pin problem either — the two things this bead named as the next step are both ruled out.

REPRODUCED FROM SCRATCH (the live instance had gone stale: kb-b82 has since been
closed, so img-n7g showing ready is now correct).

Throwaway repo, prefix aaa, a foreign zzz-001 imported open, edge added with
bd dep add:
  - bd dep tree: aaa-4iz [BLOCKED] by zzz-001 (open)
  - bd ready: lists aaa-4iz anyway
  - --explain: '1 blocker(s) resolved. Resolved blockers: zzz-001' — while
    listing zzz-001 as ready one line above. Self-contradictory in one screen.

THE VARIABLE IS THE PREFIX, NOT THE PULL. This bead conflated the two; separated
by importing a bead with the NATIVE prefix. That one blocks correctly. So
beads-pull.sh is not implicated, and a same-prefix control blocks correctly too.

NOT A VERSION ISSUE. Upstream #4647 has it root-caused in source: isCrossPrefixDep
buckets the edge as DepTargetExternal — the same bucket as an 'external:' GitHub
URL — and bd ready's materialised is_blocked column never consults it. Confirmed
present at v1.1.0 and main, still open. #5784 reports the same on v1.1.2, which is
what the newest release (1.2.2) actually is, so no upgrade available today fixes
it.

RESOLUTION. The workaround this bead proposed is now the documented rule in
CLAUDE.md next to 'bd ready is the source of truth': a cross-prefix edge is
documentation only, state the ordering in the description too.

SPUN OUT: img-4r2 (P1). Chasing the version question turned up that we pin 1.2.1,
which upstream retracted as accidental and untested, and that it migrated our
databases to a schema the tested line refuses to open.

title: Route curation-scoped lessons out of the system prompt into a LEARNED.md overlay
description:
Cited in ADR 0008. `kb-curator` ships in the image and is therefore unwritable,
which left curation-scoped lessons exactly one home - the system prompt, on
every turn - which is the cost the routing rule exists to avoid.

Shipped: an image skill now keeps an overlay at
`memory/skills/<skill>/LEARNED.md`, seeded by the same bootstrap path as any
other file, carrying no frontmatter so it is data rather than a second skill
competing for the router's attention.

Reconstructed from ADR 0008 and closed as already delivered.

title: Eval-gate a candidate skill by replaying the turn that produced the signal
description:
Cited in ADR 0008 as the proposal that would close the largest gap in bounded
self-evolution as shipped: replay the turn that produced a signal against the
candidate skill, and accept the edit only if the replay improves.

Reconstructed from ADR 0008. Until this exists, the only gate on a self-edit is
a human noticing and clicking Revert, which is exactly as strong as how closely
`memory/evolution.md` is read.

Depends on kb-3sv: this is further Stage 3 investment, and kb-3sv asks whether
the signals justify any.

title: Decide where MCP server config lives
description:
Rescoped (was: MCP management incl. UI and OAuth). This bead is now only the blocking half — the config-location decision. The UI/surfacing/OAuth half moved downstream of kb-b82.

kb-b82 proposes adding a Google Calendar server to .claude/settings.json, but that route does not exist in this deployment: agent.py sets setting_sources=[] (multi-tenant isolation) and strict_mcp_config=True (so the agent cannot grant itself servers via a .mcp.json in its writable cwd). The only live path is the mcp_servers= dict at agent.py:573, hard-coded today to hold 'ask'. So no MCP server can be added at all until this is answered — which is why the old kb-068 -> kb-b82 edge pointed the wrong way and has been reversed.

Scope:
- where the server list is stored (env, a KB file, the volume?)
- how it reaches mcp_servers= without reintroducing a settings source the agent can write
- whether the agent may read it, and whether it may propose changes to it

Out of scope, deliberately: UI and OAuth. Both are better designed after one real integration has bruised us.
close_reason: Answered in ADR 0015 and built: app/mcp_catalog.py. Definitions live in CATALOG in the image, secrets in the environment (an entry names its variable, never holds the value), and neither is writable at runtime. Ships empty. Server.auto_approve gives two-tier approval - unlisted tools fall through to can_use_tool. Reflection gets no catalog. /healthz reports each entry as ready or 'missing <VAR>'. kb-b82 is unblocked and is now a small diff.

title: Render SKILL.md as landing page for skill directories in KB browser
description: When a user clicks on a skill directory in the wiki/skill browser, SKILL.md should be rendered as the landing page — the same way GUIDE.md is rendered when a wiki folder is selected. Other contents of a skill directory (references, hooks) would be listed alongside or below. This makes skills self-documenting at a glance.

title: Persist chat history locally with session continuity
description: User wants chat history saved so within the same browser window/session, prior messages are not lost on page reload. Past sessions should be browsable and resumable. Design doc written at wiki/designs/session-management.md — covers storage options (local-first with server sync recommended), session list UI, auto-titling, and stretch goal of inline comments. See Section G for open questions. User should have an explicit 'New chat' option to start fresh.
close_reason: Delivered by docs/decisions/0017: conversations persist across reload (GET /api/conversations/{id}/events replays the whole history), are browsable via the conversation picker, and New Chat starts fresh. Auto-titling and inline comments from the original design doc were not built; filed separately.

title: Single-page layout: chat and wiki/skill view side-by-side
description: User wants to navigate the wiki and skill views without leaving the chat or losing chat history. Currently switching to the KB browser is a separate view. Goal: make the wiki/skill panel accessible from the same page as chat (e.g. a side panel or tabbed layout within the same page) so edits and browsing are visible alongside the conversation.
close_reason: Delivered by docs/decisions/0016 (one page, three panes) and carried forward by 0017: chat, wiki tree and renderer share one page, and chat history now also survives navigating between them.

title: Full-text search over conversation_events
description: docs/decisions/0017 added a durable conversation_events table (Postgres) but no search over it. A Postgres FTS index over rows where kind IN ('text','text_delta','user_message') would answer 'what did we say about X' without going through the KB, which is deliberately curated long-term memory rather than a search index. Phase 5 backlog item from the design behind 0017.

title: Presence and typing indicators for shared conversations
description: docs/decisions/0017 built the household-shared conversation stream but did not wire up presence. app/conversations.py's Conversation already has the subscriber-wake mechanism (the same asyncio.Event waiter list turns.Turn used) that a 'presence' event could reuse trivially - see the Consequences section of the ADR. Deferred for time, not difficulty.

title: No reminder reaches anyone when a connected service is about to expire
description:
img-xak made /healthz and the chat page report 'expiring' with a days_left
countdown, which is as far as it goes: somebody has to open the page or query the
endpoint. There is no scheduler in app/ - the Conception gap ADR 0011 names - so
nothing chases the human whose laptop and browser the re-auth actually needs.

Cheapest real options, roughly in order of effort:
  * a Fly cron / scheduled machine that GETs /healthz and posts elsewhere on
    state != ready
  * an external uptime checker with a JSON assertion on mcp_catalog
  * the app emailing the household account through its own gmail entry - which it
    cannot do, since the five sending tools are denied (ADR 0015). Worth noting
    because it looks like the obvious answer and is closed on purpose.

Only worth building while the account is a consumer @gmail.com on Testing. A
Workspace seat with user type Internal removes the seven-day clock and most of the
reason for this bead - but not all of it, since revocation and a disabled client
have no date attached.

title: This repo has no Stop guard on its own Claude Code sessions
description:
app/guards.py:stop_guard refuses to end a PRODUCT turn whose reply defers work
without a matching bd command. docs/decisions/0007 explains why: a prompt said
the right thing and the agent did something else anyway, and the ledger silently
lost exactly the work it exists to hold (kb-3cl).

This repo has no .claude/ directory, so nothing enforces the same rule on the
Claude Code sessions that DEVELOP it. Observed rather than theorised: a session
surfaced two pieces of discovered work in its closing message (the core.hooksPath
defect and the stale bd export instruction) and filed neither until the human
asked. Same failure, same reason, no guard.

Note the asymmetry that makes this possible: the product sets setting_sources=[]
so it cannot read .claude/settings.json, which is why its guards are Python
objects. Claude Code working in this repo DOES read that file, so a Stop hook
here is a few lines rather than a port.

Scope: a .claude/settings.json with a Stop hook that looks for deferral language
in the final message and no bd invocation in the turn. Cheap version: a shell
hook grepping the transcript. Consider also whether it belongs in this repo at
all versus the user's global config - the rule is about this ledger, so probably
here.

Do not over-build. The guard's own lesson (docs/decisions/0007) is that a bare
denial drove the agent to invent a workaround, so it must state the alternative.

title: Confirm whether bd export is still a manual step before committing
description:
CLAUDE.md says:

  **Before committing ledger changes**, run `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`.
  [...] `beads-pull.sh` does this for you; a bead you create or close by hand
  does not.

But beads installed a pre-commit hook (.beads/hooks/pre-commit, see the sibling
bead about core.hooksPath) and an export is the obvious thing for it to do. If it
does, that instruction is stale and every session is running a redundant command
- harmless, but it is the kind of stale instruction that makes a reader doubt the
rest of the file.

Check what .beads/hooks/pre-commit actually does, then either delete the
paragraph or keep it and say WHY it is still needed (e.g. the hook only exports
when the Dolt db is dirty, or it is skipped under BD_GIT_HOOK).

Note the two beads interact: if core.hooksPath gets dropped to fix the other one,
beads' pre-commit stops firing and this instruction becomes load-bearing again.
close_reason:
Measured, and the instruction is NOT stale — the opposite of this bead's hypothesis.

bd's pre-commit hook does not export. In a throwaway repo with issues.jsonl
tracked: created a bead, committed an unrelated file, and the second bead was
absent from the JSONL while the hook reported success and the commit contained
only that file.

The mechanism is the second option this bead guessed. `bd hooks run` exports
BD_GIT_HOOK=1 and auto-export refuses under it:
  auto-export: skipping — running as git hook
Unconditionally, too: it still refuses with `export.auto: true`, a setting that
demonstrably works outside a hook (it wrote all three beads on the next
`bd create`). So no config change makes the hook do this.

Kept the paragraph and said why, per this bead's own instruction. Also recorded
why export.auto stays off: the export still needs `git add`, so a manual step
remains either way, and it prints a 'no Dolt remote configured' warning on every
write.

The interaction this bead flagged did not arise — img-bl4 shared the hook file
rather than dropping core.hooksPath, so beads' hooks still fire.

title: Scope savepoints per user so concurrent turns can actually run
description:
The half of img-lsp that admission control does not solve.

img-lsp is closed because overlapping turns are now refused: Registry.begin
admits one turn at a time, so two turns can no longer savepoint over each
other. That removes the corruption. It does not remove the constraint - the
household is now strictly one turn at a time across every caller, and a second
person's message is answered with a 409 while the first person's turn runs.

kb.create_savepoint is 'git add -A' and a commit over the single shared
workspace at $KB_MOUNT/memory. Scoping a savepoint to the paths one user's
turn actually touched - or to a per-user subtree - is what would let two turns
run at once without either one's revert rolling back the other's work.

ADR 0009 names this as the ceiling that has to go before a second machine could
ever help, and its amendment records that the ceiling moved rather than lifted.

Worth doing only if the refusal actually bites in practice. Two household
members rarely collide, and a 409 that nobody ever sees is not a problem worth
this much machinery. Check the logs for refusals before starting.

title: MCP management UI: surfacing, add/remove, and per-user OAuth
description:
The downstream half of the old kb-068, which was split because its config-location question blocked kb-b82 rather than following it. That half now lives in kb-068; this is what genuinely wants a real integration first.

Scope:
- how the user adds/removes/authenticates a server (UI form vs editing whatever kb-068 settles on)
- how available servers are surfaced in the chat or skill view
- per-user OAuth: there is no token store and no callback route today, and MCP_IDENTITY_EMAIL means every /mcp turn acts as one identity, so 'per-user' is not yet a thing the app can express

Blocked by kb-b82 on purpose: design this after Google Calendar has been wired up once, not before.
--- Unblocked, and the OAuth half is now the interesting half (2026-08-17) ---

kb-b82 shipped, so this is workable. What that integration taught:

AUTH IS LAPTOP-ONLY TODAY, for two separate reasons.
1. Incidental: both packages' `auth` commands listen on localhost:3000, so in
   the container Google redirects the USER's browser to the user's own machine
   and the code never arrives. Same topology dead-end as manage-accounts.
2. Structural: `fly secrets set` restarts the machine and _materialise reads the
   environment at boot. There is no route for a token to reach a live container.

WHAT A UI FLOW NEEDS
- a WEB application OAuth client, not Desktop, with
  https://app.memory-agent.net/oauth/google/callback registered. That URL is
  reachable from a browser - unlike container localhost - and already sits
  behind Cloudflare Access.
- the callback route itself.
- a token store. The app has none. NOT the KB: agent-writable, served by
  /api/kb/file, captured in savepoints and git. So Postgres or the volume.

WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN CONVENIENCE, AND REPRICES img-xak
On a consumer account refresh tokens die every 7 days. Today recovering means:
find a laptop, run scripts/google-auth.sh, run fly secrets set, wait for a
restart. With a UI flow it is one click while already in the app. That moves the
7-day clock from disqualifying to mildly annoying, which makes the Workspace
seat in img-xak optional rather than the only way to have working Gmail. Read
the two beads together.

TWO REAL COSTS
- Minting tokens ourselves means OWNING the file formats the packages' own
  `auth` commands currently produce: @cocal wants {"<accountMode>": {...google
  tokens..., cached_email}} with accountMode defaulting to normal, @klodr wants
  {"tokens": {...}, "scopes": [...]}. Both simple, both internal and
  unversioned. Known from reading the source, NOT from a working call - the
  container probe used a fake shape and tools/list succeeded anyway, so it
  proved nothing about the format. See img-df9.
- docs/decisions/0015's spine is that a human grants capability through a
  reviewed deploy. A UI button is still a human, so the spine holds - but the
  credential moves out of `fly secrets` into storage this app writes. That
  wants its own ADR, not a drive-by.

SEQUENCING: do not start before ~2026-08-24. Let the first real expiry decide
between this and the Workspace seat; both are cheap to act on afterwards and
guessing now is not.

title: Work deferred in chat was lost before the Stop guard existed
description:
Cited in CLAUDE.md as the bead the ledger lost: a turn deferred work into chat
("a follow-up for a later session") without filing it, and the work went
nowhere.

**Its content is unrecoverable.** The original bead was never on the Fly ledger
- prod has no record of it, closed or otherwise - and the local ledger it lived
in was destroyed by a `docker compose down -v`. This bead is a marker so the
citation resolves, not a reconstruction: nothing here should be read as a
recovered description, because there is none.

Closed because the defect it demonstrates was fixed: the Stop guard in
app/guards.py now refuses to end a turn whose reply defers work without a `bd`
command to match. See ADR 0007.
close_reason: the defect is fixed by the Stop guard; the original content is unrecoverable

title: Add Google Calendar MCP integration
description:
Connect Google Calendar so the agent can read and manage household events.

kb-068 is answered (ADR 0015): server definitions live in CATALOG in
app/mcp_catalog.py, credentials in the environment, and neither is writable at
runtime. The old plan here - 'add the MCP server config to .claude/settings.json'
- is impossible in this deployment and has been removed.

What is left:

1. Pick a Google Calendar MCP server package and PIN its version, for the reason
   the Dockerfile pins bd. Bake it into the image rather than npx-ing at runtime.
2. Set up OAuth against a dedicated HOUSEHOLD Google account, and have each
   person share their calendar with it. A refresh token belongs to one account
   and reaches only calendars shared with it; consumer Gmail has no domain-wide
   delegation. Credentials are household-shared by decision, not oversight - see
   ADR 0015 - so enabling this enables it for everyone.
3. Add one Server(...) entry to CATALOG. Put READ-shaped tools in auto_approve
   and leave writes out, so creating or deleting an event falls through to
   can_use_tool and a person clicks Allow.
4. fly secrets set the variables the entry names. Until they are set the server
   is dropped from every turn and /healthz reports it as 'missing <VAR>'.

The mechanism is built, tested and shipped empty, so this is now a small diff.
close_reason:
Built: Google Calendar and Gmail are the two CATALOG entries in
app/mcp_catalog.py, both pointing at one household Google account through one
OAuth client. Three secrets, produced by scripts/google-auth.sh.

Three things contradicted ADR 0015's assumptions and are recorded as an
amendment there rather than quietly fixed:

- secrets names a VALUE; Google credentials are FILES. Server.files +
  _materialise write them to MCP_STATE_DIR once per process (the servers write
  refreshed tokens back, so per-turn would discard the refresh).
- Gmail cannot use the household-hub model Calendar uses. A token reaches only
  its own mailbox; consumer delegation is web-UI only and the API answers 403
  Delegation denied. So it reads the household account's OWN inbox, and
  forwarding filters are what make that useful.
- gmail.compose grants SENDING - one scope, not two, measured by booting the
  server at each scope. Hence Server.deny, a third tier feeding
  disallowed_tools. Verified rather than assumed: a live test drives the real
  CLI with a stub server whose handler records whether it was entered, and deny
  wins even over an explicit allowed_tools entry.

Node is now pinned and checksummed too - the Gmail server wants >=22.23.1,
Debian ships v20, and npm warns and installs anyway. Image got smaller:
1.57GB -> 1.53GB.

Follow-up filed as img-df9 (re-measure the tool inventory on version bumps).
